card.name: Words before how long or how fast to act
card.fires_on: Small words such as to, long, of, as or used inside instructions about how long, how quickly or in what manner to do a step. Often the word comes just before a time limit or a manner term like soon, promptly, or a good job.

modes.label: How long to do something
modes.description: The word comes right before or inside a phrase about duration of an action, like scrubbing hands.
modes.example: Here’s a little trick you can use to remember how long<< to>> scrub: Sing the "happy birthday"

modes.label: Time limits in preparation steps
modes.description: Linking words in drug preparation or transfer steps that set how soon or how continuously a step is finished.
modes.example: a maximum time of 8 hours from initial closure entry is permitted to<< complete>> fluid transfer operation.

modes.label: Manner of doing a step
modes.description: A word just before a manner term like soon, technique or a good job in plain instructions.
modes.example: Encourage the patient to void<< as>> soon as the imaging study is completed and

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about doing something once, in one go, or quickly, and away from words about ongoing monitoring or running.
card.plain: It fires on little words in instructions that tell you how long or how quickly to carry out a step.
